newsitem.title: USA: Pennzoil sets $460 mln 1997 capital budget.
newsitem.headline: Pennzoil sets $460 mln 1997 capital budget.

text.p: Pennzoil Co has approved a 1997 capital budget of $460 million, the company said.

The company's chairman and chief executive officer, James Pate, said in an announcement that $338 million would be spent on oil and gas, $98 million on motor oil and refined products and $24 million on franchise operations and other projects.
Pennzoil said the overall capital budget in 1997 is $105 million less than estimated 1996 capital spending of 565 million and would be well within its operating cash flow.

The 1997 budget increases oil and gas spending by eight percent, or $24 million, the statement said. The company will offset this by an anticipated $134 million decline in capital spending on motor oil and refined products, primarily due to the completion of the upgrade to its Shreveport, La., refinery in early 1997.

In the statement Pate said the company would be placing a strong emphasis on strategic growth initiatives aimed at making Pennzoil a global oil and gas producer. He added the company would be entering a new exploration phase this year.

Pennzoil plans to drill eight exploration wells in Azerbaijan, Egypt, Qatar and Australia. The company said international oil and gas expenditures will total $66 million, or 20 percent of the 1997 budget. The domestic oil and gas budget is about $272 million and will emphasize exploitation and development drilling along with increased exploration.
Pennzoil's two strategic refining projects, the Excel Paralubes joint venture with DuPont Co's Conoco unit and the Shreveport refinery upgrade, will be operational during 1997's first quarter.
These two projects are expected to contribute approximately $0.50 per share of earnings and $45 million of after-tax cash flow in 1997.
